variedades.ARBORIO: Italian short, rounded grain variety with a lot of starch. It is the typical rice for risotto.
variedades.BASMATI: Aromatic long, slender grain rice, grown mainly in India and Pakistan. It lengthens when cooked and stays loose.
variedades.IPSALA: Variety from Turkey, grown in the Ipsala area (Edirne province), in the northwest of the country.
variedades.JASMINE: Aromatic long grain rice from Thailand. When cooked it is soft and slightly sticky.
variedades.KARACADAG: Local variety from southeastern Turkey, from the area of Mount Karacadağ (Diyarbakır).

proyecto.intro: The models on this page are the result of the project's 6 artificial intelligence topics. Each card sums up what was done and its main result, measured on photos the models never saw during training.

t1.texto: 70/15/15 split without data leakage (train 52,292 · validation 11,205 · test 11,206), saved as CSV for reproducibility. A generator that loads photos batch by batch and a conditional GAN that generates grains per variety.

t2.texto: Hyperband searched the model, learning rate, batch size, dropout and epochs, dropping early whatever did not look promising. The pretrained models needed very low learning rates, around 0.00001.

t3.texto: K-fold, stratified k-fold, hold-out and Monte Carlo were compared. Leave-one-out, leave-p-out and time series were ruled out with a justification. Cross-validation revealed that EfficientNet was unstable.

t4.texto: 3 CNNs (custom, EfficientNetB0, ResNet50V2) and 2 transformers (ViT-B/16, DeiT-S), all above 99%. On this dataset the transformers did not beat the CNNs.

t5.texto: Homogeneous (3 CNNs), heterogeneous (all 5) and hybrid (stacking). The best one fixes 2 photos compared with ResNet50V2, but McNemar's test shows it is not significant (p = 0.5).

t6.texto: Distributed training on 2 GPUs with MirroredStrategy. With FedAvg and 5 clients, the federated model reached 98.1% (IID case) without any client sharing its photos.
